reasoning: docs/DESIGN.md R12 + open decision 4. Today `ask` surfaces ONE next subject and `status` names the thin decisions, but nothing closes the loop: a low-confidence decision never becomes the specific next question, and nothing enforces a ceiling on how many questions a run may ask. The skill's governor says the budget is real, so the program must enforce it rather than trust the agent. Scope: (a) pick the thinnest decision(s), (b) derive the specific follow-up question, (c) JEV `already_answered` gate before asking, (d) a run ceiling with an explicit budget-thin marker, (e) write the question row so the branch is trackable. Acceptance: a run with a 0.41-confidence decision produces a named follow-up question, refuses one JEV scores as already answered (>= 0.55), and stops at the ceiling with `budget-thin: true` recorded rather than silently truncating.
title: [P1] the feedback engine: turn low-confidence decisions into the next question batch, bounded by a budget governor

reasoning: docs/DESIGN.md - the engine shape. The question->answer->question tree currently has no edges: `decision.question_id` exists but nothing populates it, and there is no way to ask which questions a decision closed or which new questions it opened. Without those edges the cascade cannot be walked, so depth cannot be reported honestly and a branch cannot be shown as closed. Scope: populate question_id on answer, add a `closes` list on the decision, add a walk that reports open branches and their depth. Acceptance: after answering, the decision names the question it closed; `status` reports open-branch count and max depth from the stored edges alone (no inference from prose).
title: [P1] branch linking: record that THIS answer closes THAT question, and follow the chain when a resolved answer spawns a new branch

reasoning: tests/smoke.sh proves the loop end to end (15 assertions, green) but it is a shell script: it cannot assert on internal behaviour, it leaves its namespace behind, and it cannot run a single case. The verbs are the API now that the repo is public, so they need real regression coverage. reasoning: docs/SPEC-001-graph.md sections 2 and 3. The engine reasons over relationships and there is nowhere to store them: today only decision.question_id exists and nothing populates it. One generic edge table rather than one per relationship, because DuckBrain declared tables need explicit columns and never introspect, so a narrow fixed shape keeps new edge kinds from forcing a mid-run migration. Columns: id(E-###### fixed-width), project_id, kind(opens|closes|satisfies|affects|breaks|derives_from|references|blocks), src_kind, src_id, dst_kind, dst_id, confidence(double, -1 when asserted by a person or rule rather than a model call), source(gate|impact|human|rule), note, created_at. Plus the facet table (F-######, project_id, question_id, facet(data|failure|ownership|cost|test|who_else), status, closed_by, note). Acceptance: `auger init` declares both tables idempotently and the live namespace exposes them at /api/ns/auger/tables; an edge round-trips through the declared-table API with its kind/confidence/source intact; inserting an edge whose src_id does not exist is REFUSED rather than silently stored.
title: [P1] add the graph tables (edge, facet) and declare them in the namespace — SPEC-001 2/3

reasoning: docs/SPEC-001-graph.md section 4 BEAT 4 and section 5. This is the mechanic that closes branches, and the engine is not one without it. When a question becomes answered|linked|moot: (a) every question with a derives_from edge from it is re-examined - if its blockers are resolved and it is now answerable from existing evidence it is GATED and linked rather than asked, otherwise it becomes newly askable; (b) when a decision is invalidated by a breaks edge, every question that decision closed becomes moot with the reason recorded, and that change propagates recursively. Engineering calls already concluded in the spec: branches DO reopen automatically when the answer that closed them is invalidated, with the reason recorded, because a stale closed branch silently reads as done and is worse than an open one. Acceptance: a question whose parent decision is invalidated by a breaks edge becomes moot with a reason naming the edge; the cascade reaches grandchildren; a question with an unresolved `blocks` edge is never surfaced by ask; a question that becomes answerable after a parent closes is LINKED by the gate rather than asked.
title: [P1] propagation: closure and moot cascades — SPEC-001 BEAT 4
